implementationNotes: STATE AT 2026-11-10 (verify against the live tracker and repository first; this note is a pointer, not authority; restore with the opum-handoff skill, the cursor is never authoritative). REFS: origin/dev == origin/main == d82e3d90ff9a85d10ae49b7fa5ad1f93c1964496 before this handoff PR lands (promoted via opum-ai/ward-cli#328); newest tag v0.1.1, no release cut. No open PR, no uncommitted or stashed edits. DONE THIS SESSION: WCLI-21 slice 2b-2 (unsealKey, #323, 461bca3, two Opus rounds), slice 3a (#326, e5b9cb9: one contract code per Tpm2Reason with tpm_* catalog entries, NB6 split session_not_encrypted vs tool_incompatible, key_not_sealed on ENOENT only, lone .priv = key_incomplete with setup refusing, key_exists, exact two-line sessionconfig parse, NB1-NB3, cleanup removes .priv first, a refused stdout kills the child; two Opus rounds by ward-cli-review-326), tracker PRs #322 #324 #327, promotion #325 and #328. NEXT, NOT STARTED: slice 3b. It needs a dispatch floor and a FENCE FROM THE LEADER before any commit; wait for CLEAR. 3b scope (DEC-262 a15/a16, recorded verbatim on WCLI-21): the leaked-session behaviour (flush fails AFTER a successful unseal: return the key, one structured warning, no retry loop, never flush a handle not created; flush fails after a FAILED unseal: report the unseal error with the flush failure as detail; doctor reports the visible saved-session handle count as an attention state that does not fail doctor, naming reset or reboot as what clears it) and the doctor states (s1 unsupported, s2 access refused, s3 not user-private, tool_untrusted naming the path, tool_incompatible naming the tpm2-tools version, key_incomplete, plus a state for blobs unloadable after tpm2_clear), reading Tpm2Error.detail not the WardError. CARRIED INTO 3b: N1 (an EEXIST on the .pub link currently gives key_exists although a lone .pub is not a sealed key: give key_exists only on the .priv link). N3 (a) the provider boundary must translate tpm_key_not_sealed to vault_key_missing or teach setup.ts and reporting.ts observeKey the TPM codes and must NEVER treat tpm_key_incomplete as missing; (c) the 3d presence check must count a lone .priv as the TPM holds a key; (d) the tool_incompatible and tool_untrusted doctor states read Tpm2Error.detail. Do not wire a tpm_* code into a live path before observeKey has its cases. N2 (the classifier accepts the vocabulary tokens in any order though tpm2-tools prints a fixed bit order) is ROUTED TO opum-doc by the leader and UNTOUCHED: do not change it. THEN 3c (the lore ADR under docs/adr/, through lore, lore check must exit 0: RUNPATH residual, shebang rules as built, the leaked-session behaviour, the #316 primary template and attribute set as part of the stored-format contract under DEC-255 a6) and 3d (the wiring that replaces the 7 createKeychainKeyProvider sites in src/cli/main.ts, built to (a16) selection rules 1 to 5; cleared in principle, needs its own fence). Each PR at most about 400 lines (#326 ran to +574 and was accepted once; tell the leader early); at each green head create a detached review worktree .claude/worktrees/ward-cli-review-<N> and report to the leader; nothing merges before an Opus verdict is recorded; promotion goes with the last slice-3 PR. The other open items: WCLI-157 PARTLY MET (needs a real-output measurement), WCLI-158 (timed-out tool must let the CLI exit and kill the grandchild, owed to slice 3 at the latest), WCLI-159, WCLI-160 DO NOT START, WCLI-162, WCLI-82 and WCLI-92 (wait on the marketplace pin), WCLI-120 (waits on a real tag push; release is the operator's to cut). NB4 (a timeout finally can run before the killed child exits, so a saved session never written to disk may be stranded) is for the 3b design. WORKTREES (DEC-208, LCLI-740 open: do NOT remove, deregister or prune any): every one under .claude/worktrees/, including ward-cli-review-323, 323b, 326, 326b, 326c, and the older ones. JETSON PROBE TERMS (the leader authorises each probe; four were run on 2026-11-09 and all are recorded on WCLI-21): reach the host only through the mesh launcher ~/.scripts/jetson (never bare ssh), piping a script with sh -s; TPM2TOOLS_TCTI=device:/dev/tpmrm0 (the kernel resource manager) only; a throwaway primary and no real key, no unseal unless the leader says so; bounded, in a mktemp directory removed by a trap; compare tpm2_getcap handles-transient, handles-persistent, handles-saved-session and handles-loaded-session before and after (empty both times so far); record commands, verbatim outputs and the handle diff on WCLI-21 and report them to the leader. NO BINARY GOES TO THE JETSON BEFORE SLICE 4. Slice 4 (T26 harness and runbook, includes an operator reboot) and slice 5 (advertise Linux; may touch the release path: stop and report before committing) follow slice 3. HABITS THAT PAID: batch tracker writes before a promotion; run gh pr merge and git push each bare in its own call with --match-head-commit and the full SHA; a review round at a new head needs a new detached worktree (the ownership guard refuses moving one); prove each blocker both ways with a mutation run against a saved copy of the source in the scratchpad and restore it.
